newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index rises 0.74 pts in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index rises 0.74 pts in thin trading.

text.p: Major Slovak shares were mixed in listless trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Friday, with gains to shares of refinery Slovnaft pushing the index up 0.74 points to 185.57.
"It seems that the activity has removed to the field of direct trading, leaving the floor a bit empty at the presence," Radovan Dzugas of Creditanstalt said.
Only 867 shares were traded on the BSE's listed floor, while 5.6 million shares changed hands through block and direct deals.
Dzugas said the market has been suffering from a lack of domestic investors, who would play with smaller volumes, while foreign investors so far appeared to find market liquidity low.
Steel maker VSZ closed down 34 crowns at 620, with only 35 traded shares, while the most heavily-weighted issue, oil refiner Slovnaft closed up 20 crowns at 810.
"I think Slovnaft will rise a bit further in near future, as it has been supported by some direct deals in these days," Dzugas said.
Overall volume increased to 5,610,947 traded shares, from 432,469 shares traded on Thursday, while turnover rose to 909.34 million crowns from 181.75 million.
